project.title: Rijksmuseum Group Hunt
project.description: A collaborative scavenger hunt for teenagers visiting the Rijksmuseum in groups: a web app opened from a QR code, with quiz elements and a group AI chat.
project.introText: A collaborative scavenger hunt through the Rijksmuseum for visitors aged 12 to 18 who come in a group, with quiz elements and a group AI chat. It is the Data Systems Project of the MSc Information Studies at the University of Amsterdam (2026/27), for the Rijksmuseum with Q42 and Curamando, and still in progress.

gridImages.caption: Three phones from the halte prototype: the launcher for player, host and the design system, the player's start screen, and the host setting up a ride by group (school class or family), level (12 to 14 or 15 to 18), a route of 5, 8 or 12 stops, a time to be back and a meeting point.

The group's A0 ideation poster, which I designed: “Creating Meaningful Interactions in the Museum Space”, with our research question about teenage visitors, the target user and the route over the museum floors.
One ride on the player's phone, screen by screen: joining, the stops and their hints, points for each find, and the mystery painting revealed tile by tile.

project.middleText: Teams of teenagers, with an adult host, follow hints from artwork to artwork. Each find earns one tile of a hidden mystery painting, such as Vermeer's Woman Reading a Letter, revealed bit by bit; the full painting is the last stop, where all teams meet. Hints are unlimited: the first is free, and each extra one lowers what the stop is worth, a team can always say “I can't find it”, and quiz questions and a group AI chat run alongside. There are no timers and no points for speed: points come from looking and finding. Two levels serve ages 12 to 14 and 15 to 18, and a leaderboard closes the visit. Visitors open the hunt as a web app from a QR code. I made the A0 ideation poster and four visual identity directions for the app, each built as a clickable prototype; halte was chosen.
project.context: Data Systems Project, MSc Information Studies (University of Amsterdam), 2026/27, with Q42 and Curamando as stakeholders

summary.brief: What makes a visit inside the Rijksmuseum rich, and which interface choices support it; we focused on teenagers who come in a group.
summary.role: Designer and researcher in a team of five; my part so far: the A0 ideation poster and four visual identity directions, each a clickable prototype.
summary.method: A persona (Rick, 12 to 18, visiting in a group), ideation on an A0 poster, game design, and four visual identity directions built as clickable prototypes.
summary.outcome: In progress (2026/27): a game design for the hunt and a chosen visual identity, halte.

facts: year-olds visiting in groups, on two levels: 12 to 14 and 15 to 18
visual identity directions, each built as a clickable prototype
timers on a stop: points come from looking and finding, not from speed
project.shows: Interaction design for a group in a gallery, where the AI chat is one part of a shared game rather than the whole interface.
project.highlightCaption: My halte prototypes for player and host: the player joins the Gallery of Honour line from the host's QR code at stop 1 of 8, and the host's phone explains what teams do at a stop: read the hint, put the phone down and look up, show the find by photo or name, then answer one question.
